note_2026_08_10:
Session was a mobile pass over /delivery driven entirely by the shop sending phone screenshots, plus a 4-column events grid. Five commits, all pushed (c0bb789, 511c270, 6b3fd17, 726a282, e6ed8bb).

  (0) HOW TO ACTUALLY SEE THE ORDER FLOW LOCALLY — this unblocks everything else and was the missing trick in previous sessions. Steps 2-6 sit behind a LINE login that redirects to access.line.me, which the in-app Browser pane refuses to load. Fix: blank NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFF_ID in love-pier-main/.env.local (back it up first), wait ~6s for the dev server to restart, and handleStart() falls through to setStep('distance') because isLiffConfigured() is false. Then the distance step's own 'โหมดทดสอบระยะทาง' toggle exposes 'จำลอง: อยู่ในรัศมี', which fakes the GPS result and lets you reach menu -> summary -> payment. RESTORE .env.local AFTERWARDS. Do not press the final 'สั่งซื้อและชำระเงิน' — it creates a real order and pushes a LINE card.

  (a) THE CART BUTTON HID THE LAST MENU ITEM (c0bb789) — a real functional bug, not cosmetic. Once the cart has anything in it, MenuExperience renders a `fixed bottom-6 right-5` cart pill. The menu list reserved no room for it, so at the very bottom of the page the LAST card's 'เพิ่มลงตะกร้า' sat underneath the pill with no scroll left to move it clear: that item could not be added at all on a phone. Proved with elementFromPoint on the button's centre (covered:true, atBottom:true), fixed with `pb-28` applied only when showAddToCart is on, so /menu is untouched.

  (b) STEPHEADER TAP TARGETS (511c270). The ‹ and ✕ were the bare glyph's 20x32 box, under the 24px minimum, and they are the only way back or out of the wizard on every step. Now w-6 h-6 flex-centred.

  (c) THE SHOP'S REAL COMPLAINT TOOK THREE ROUNDS TO PIN DOWN, and the lesson is to ask early rather than guess. 'ให้เวลาดูในมือถือเห็นดีไซน์ครบ' was ambiguous between 'the photo is cropped', 'the text is illegible', and 'content is below the fold'. An AskUserQuestion returned 'เนื้อหาข้างล่างต้องเลื่อนถึงจะเห็น'. Then they sent the SAME screenshot with a red circle drawn around the seam between the cream block and the black footer — i.e. the half-cut black band peeking at the bottom edge read as an unfinished page. Measured: 28px of cream padding + the footer's own 48px pt-12 = ~76px of dead band right at the fold.

  (d) FIT + POLISH OF THE WELCOME SCREEN (6b3fd17 then 726a282). PageHero gained a `compact` mode used ONLY by the delivery welcome; the six marketing pages that share it are untouched and still 260px with their eyebrow and dots. Compact: drops the 'LOVE PIER BEACH CAFE' eyebrow (it landed exactly on the Love Pier sign in the 3D render and was unreadable — and the craft floor bans eyebrows outright), drops the 8 slide dots (picking a photo is not a task on this screen), takes a smaller title, and runs a heavier scrim (from-black/70 via-black/35) so white type survives bright sand. The welcome block became `min-h-[calc(100dvh-var(--nav-h,64px))] sm:min-h-0` with the CTA on `mt-auto`, so the footer starts at or below the fold instead of peeking, and the button sits in thumb reach with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) under it. The h2 went 24px -> clamp(28px,8vw,34px) light so the OFFER outranks the hero caption (it was 36px vs 24px — hierarchy was inverted), and the three step markers went from solid cocoa discs to hairline outlines so the button is now the only cocoa mass on the screen, per DESIGN.md's 'cocoa is the colour the customer touches'.

  (e) THE SIZING LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the compact hero is sized in **vh, not vw** — `clamp(190px, 34vh, 300px)`. What squeezes this screen is a SHORT viewport (and LINE's chrome eating ~45px more), not a narrow one, so a vw clamp gave a tall phone the same 180px band as a short one and pooled the leftover as dead cream. Numbers at 402x784: dead space between the steps and the button fell 225px -> 111px while the photo grew 180 -> 267px. At 375x620 (the tightest realistic LINE viewport) everything still clears the fold.

  (f) A FLEXBOX DEAD END, recorded so it is not retried: the first attempt let the hero and the copy both be `flex-1` so the photo would absorb the slack. It failed twice — `height:100%` on the hero computed to 0px because a percentage height resolves against the parent's `height`, which is `auto` when the parent is sized by flex/min-height; and after switching to `self-stretch`, the two flex-1 siblings did not split the space as predicted (the hero stayed pinned at its min-height while the copy took 515px). The vh clamp in (e) is deterministic and replaced the whole approach.

  (g) EVENTS FOUR TO A ROW (e6ed8bb), asked for directly by the shop. components/events/EventCard.js already declared `sizes="(min-width:1024px) 25vw"` — the card was built for a four-up grid and only the grid class in pages/events.js was ever left at `sm:grid-cols-2`. Now 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 across sm, md, lg on BOTH the Upcoming and Past grids, verified as `276px x 4` at a 1280px viewport, and the sizes hint gained the matching 33vw step. CAVEAT TOLD TO THE SHOP: only 1 upcoming event exists, so a 4-column grid renders one smaller card and three empty slots.

  (h) FOUND AND REPORTED, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — the shop has not chosen yet: form labels in the order summary and payment steps are `text-black/45` at 11px on cream, measured 3.3:1 against the 4.5:1 minimum, on the checkout screens; item names in the order summary are `truncate`d so 'Pier Breakfast + กาแ…' hides what was ordered; the distance step centres a heading and a button in an otherwise empty full-height screen; StepHeader is 95% opaque so dark menu-card buttons ghost through it while scrolling. Delivery fee is still ฿0, as already recorded.
note_2026_08_06:
Session fixed the whole event-image + event-save path, then removed the /events spotlight and ran an `impeccable polish` pass on the home page. Six commits, all pushed.

  (1) HEIC UPLOAD (cbb4d6b). Shop could not upload iPhone photos to events: the image just never appeared. Two stacked causes. First, `app/api/admin/upload/route.ts` resizes with sharp, and the sharp build here has NO HEVC decoder (`sharp.format.heif.input.fileSuffix` is only ['.avif']; encoding hevc fails with 'heifsave: Unsupported compression'), so .heic 500s. Second, EventModal.handleUpload had NO catch, so the 500 was swallowed silently — it looked like 'upload finished, image missing'. Fix: `lib/upload-image.ts` now detects HEIC (mime image/heic|heif OR .heic/.heif extension — HEIC often reports an empty MIME) and converts to JPEG in the browser via heic2any before POSTing; all callers (events, promotions, menu) share this lib. EventModal got try/catch + toast on both the main image and the album loop, plus accept=".heic,.heif".

  (2) BINARY CORRUPTION ON VERCEL (40029ca) — the important one. After the HEIC fix images uploaded but rendered BROKEN, returning HTTP 200. Forensics: fetched bytes started `52494646 efbfbd...` (RIFF then U+FFFD) and the file was LARGER than a real webp. Root cause: supabase-js sends a Node `Buffer` as a raw fetch body, and the Vercel serverless runtime coerces that body to a UTF-8 string, so every byte >= 0x80 becomes EF BF BD. LOCALHOST DOES NOT REPRODUCE IT (undici handles the Buffer as binary) — a clean local test proves nothing here. Fix: pass `new Blob([new Uint8Array(webp)], {type:'image/webp'})` so supabase-js sends binary-safe multipart. The Uint8Array wrap is required because @types/node v26 rejects Buffer as a BlobPart. Applied to app/api/admin/upload/route.ts and lib/menuImport/imageProcess.ts. lib/upload-promotion-image.ts is client-side and already passed a Blob. >>> ANY IMAGE UPLOADED BEFORE 40029ca IS PERMANENTLY CORRUPT AND MUST BE RE-UPLOADED.

  (3) BLANK EVENT DATE (f99171d). Saving an event failed with a bare 'เกิดข้อผิดพลาด'. A blank date field posts '', and both routes did `body.eventDate ?? null` — '' is not nullish, so '' reached the `date` column and Postgres threw 'Invalid time value'. Changed to `|| null` in POST and PUT, wrapped insert/update in try/catch that returns the real DB message, and surfaced it in the admin toast so a failed save is no longer opaque.

  (4) REMOVED THE /events FEATURED SPOTLIGHT (c922287) at the shop's request (they crossed it out on a screenshot). Deleted the whole `{fe && <section>}` block plus everything it alone consumed: getSrcSet, the Link import, dbFeatured/fe, descKey/entrySubKey/freeLabel, and the reserve/featuredImageAlt/perPerson/freeLabel copy keys in all 3 dicts (also dropped catKey, dead beforehand). KEPT the separate centered 'THE SYMPHONY CLUB' banner above the grid — it is a different block and was not in the crossed-out area. The featured event still appears as a normal card under Upcoming/Past.

  (5) HOME PAGE POLISH (c87669a), via the impeccable skill. Biggest finding was systemic: --color-gold #c9a96e only reaches 2.02:1 on cream, and DESIGN.md's own 'Gold-on-Dark Rule' says it must never sit on light surfaces — yet pages/index.js used it for prices, section links, event titles and eyebrows everywhere. Shop chose 'add a deeper gold' over 'switch to cocoa'. Added two @theme tokens in styles/globals.css: --color-gold-deep #8c682c (4.59:1 on cream) and --color-muted-strong #67625a (5.46:1, replacing text-muted #888 at 3.20 and hardcoded #bbb labels at 1.73 — nearly invisible). 22 usages moved over; bg-gold in the black lightbox correctly left alone. GOTCHA WORTH REMEMBERING: after the edit the classes were on 30 elements but computed to rgb(26,26,26) because Tailwind had not generated the utilities yet — `next build` passing did NOT catch this, only reading computed styles in the browser did. Always verify new @theme tokens by reading getComputedStyle, not by trusting the build. Also fixed: hero dots 6x6px -> 24x40px hit areas with aria-labels/aria-current; hero autoplay now pauses on hover/focus and is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion; the 5 stacked hero images no longer repeat identical alt text; the lightbox became a real dialog (Escape, arrow keys, aria-modal, labelled controls, body scroll lock via the existing .menu-open class); the U+26F6 glyph used as an expand icon became a drawn SVG; the expand button now renders whenever an event has photos (previously only at 2+, so single-photo events had NO keyboard path); 'More' was localized; section 'view all' + phone/email links got a 24px minimum target. Refactors: the three duplicated menu sections became <MenuHighlights> (which also owns the empty case, so an empty query no longer strands a heading over nothing) and the duplicated desktop/mobile CTA became <MenuCta>. Removed 6 COPY keys that were already dead (exploreMenu, hoursValue, location, locationValue, openInMaps, since).

  (6) UPCOMING-EVENTS FILTERING + LAYOUT (c87669a then ca659eb). The section is headed 'อีเวนต์ที่กำลังจะมาถึง' but rendered any active event, so a finished event showed on the home page (shop flagged it). Now filters to events whose endDate (or eventDate) has not passed, soonest first. Per the shop's follow-up the section KEEPS ITS PLACE when nothing is upcoming and shows a localized empty state (eventsEmpty/eventsEmptySub) instead of the old hardcoded Flow Sunset fallback — which was itself past-dated and had to go. Then, asked whether multiple events should become a banner or a slideshow, I recommended NEITHER (a carousel hides events 2-3, the page already has a hero slideshow whose rhythm it would duplicate, and it would need its own pause + reduced-motion handling) and built lead + poster instead: nearest event at full width, the rest as 3:4 poster cards reusing components/events/EventCard so home and /events look like one system. Event links now point at /events/{id} rather than the generic list. Verified by temporarily padding the array to 3 events, screenshotting desktop + mobile, then removing the scaffold. NOTE: a `typeof window` branch used for that temp preview caused a hydration mismatch — the temp code, not the feature; it is gone.
note_2026_08_06_menu_publish:
Later the same day: PUBLISHED the 233 bulk-imported menu items to customers (2e4b6b3). The shop asked whether their Google Drive photo folders (one subfolder per category + the xlsx) were structured correctly, which led into the whole publish task.

  (a) IMAGE FOLDER STRUCTURE — the answer is that it does not matter. classifyImages() in lib/menuImport/imageMatch.ts strips folder names and matches on BASENAME only, and imageClient.ts accepts all three input shapes (a .zip expanded in-browser with fflate, a webkitdirectory folder pick, or a drag-drop that walks entries). So per-category subfolders are fine. The real constraints told to the shop: filenames must be UNIQUE ACROSS ALL FOLDERS (since folders are ignored, the same basename in two categories is a conflict), must equal image_code (or image_file when set), must be .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp (HEIC is rejected at match time, not converted — that is a different path from the event uploader), and must not end in ' (1)'. Recommended the FOLDER picker over .zip: expandZip does arrayBuffer()+unzipSync, i.e. the whole archive in browser memory at once, which will not survive a few hundred phone-sized originals.

  (b) WHY NOTHING SHOWED — three independent gates, all found by reading rather than guessing: categories.is_active=true in lib/db/menuPageData.js (the 10 import categories were seeded false), menu_items.is_available=true (the 21 incomplete rows are forced false), and TAB_SECTION_CATS in components/menu/menuData.js only knew the 7 hand-built categories, so even an active import category had no tab and was unreachable.

  (c) THE DUPLICATE PROBLEM. 6 of the 10 import categories shadow a legacy one (chicken-rice-1/chicken-rice, breakfast-7/breakfast, coffee-drinks/coffee+non-coffee+italian-soda, icecream/ice-cream, cake-bakery/sweets, bar-wine/alcohol); only pasta-western, sushi-roll, bbq-seafood and oyster-bar are genuinely new. Enabling all 10 without touching the old ones would have shown customers two parallel menus. Shop chose REPLACE. Result: 212 items visible (233 minus the 21 incomplete), 60 legacy items hidden.

  (d) WHAT SHIPPED. TAB_SECTION_CATS now defines 10 tabs and each one lists its import category FIRST and the legacy equivalent AFTER, so reactivating an old category later lands it in the right tab instead of creating a duplicate tab. SECTION_IDS and the tab labels are derived from that one map (TAB_LABELS replaced three hand-maintained per-language arrays). MenuExperience.js renders sections from the map in a single loop, replacing SEVEN near-identical hardcoded blocks, and hides any tab whose categories are inactive or have no items (previously such a tab was a dead scroll target, because scrollTo() silently no-ops on a missing anchor). getSrcSet learned the import path menu/<code>/960.webp — it only understood the legacy '-960w.webp' suffix — and imageVersion now flows through menuPageData.js -> buildMenuData -> withImageVersion() as a ?v= cache-buster, which matters because re-uploading an image reuses the same storage path. menuAddOnsForCategory also now answers for 'coffee-drinks' (that is why the drinks section renders 59 rows for 57 DB items: the 2 espresso add-ons).

  (e) THE TAB BAR BUG worth remembering. The sticky bar used `flex justify-center overflow-x-auto`. When the row overflows, justify-center pushes the leading items past scrollLeft:0 where NOTHING can scroll them back — measured at 375px: scrollLeft was already 0 and the first tab sat at -350px. This was latent with 9 tabs and became severe at 12. Fixed with `[&>:first-child]:ml-auto [&>:last-child]:mr-auto` instead of justify-center: auto margins centre the row while it fits and collapse to 0 once it overflows. Verified both ends reachable (+16px / -16px, i.e. exactly the px-4 padding). Also added an effect that scrolls the ACTIVE tab back into view, since 12 tabs overflow even on desktop — that effect is the one thing NOT verified in-browser, because the preview pane refuses to scroll this page (scrollTop stays 0 even via document.scrollingElement, and computer{scroll} times out with 'pane hidden').

  (f) THE SWITCH ITSELF is scripts/activate-import-categories.mjs — dry-run by default, --apply to write, --revert --apply to swap back. It defines 'imported' as category_no IS NOT NULL and 'legacy' as NULL, and only ever writes categories.is_active, so no menu_items row is edited or deleted and the revert is exact.

  (g) EMPTY IMAGE WELLS (7720352), found only by looking at the deployed site. MenuCard ALWAYS reserved a 4:3 well (`paddingTop: 75%`), so every item without a photo rendered as a ~450px blank box above three lines of text — on mobile barely one card fit per screen and the menu was effectively unusable. The well now renders only when there is an image, and the Signature badge (absolutely positioned inside the well) falls back to an inline chip in the text block. Measured on production afterwards: cards with a photo 398px, cards without 128px, and the count of `padding-top:75%` in the served HTML fell 218 -> 111.

  (h) PRODUCTION VERIFICATION, all measured on www.lovepier.cafe, not locally. Tabs/sections/counts match local exactly. The IntersectionObserver highlights the right tab when scrolled to the last section, and the bar auto-scrolls it back into view (barScrollLeft 481, activeFullyInView true) — that effect had been reported as unverified and is now CONFIRMED. Clicking a tab scrolls to its section (top=129px, i.e. clear of the nav + sticky bar) and updates the highlight. At 375px both ends of the tab bar are reachable (+16 / -16, exactly the px-4 padding). No console errors. A sample card's currentSrc resolved to `menu/1_01/960.webp?v=1`, proving the new getSrcSet path AND the image_version cache-buster both work end to end.

  (i) CORRECTION to an earlier belief in this session: the in-app Browser pane DOES scroll this page. Setting scrollTop and reading it back in the same tick returns the old value because scroll-behavior is smooth — it looked like the scroll was blocked. Await ~1-2s, or force `style.scrollBehavior='auto'` before measuring. A stale-layout race is also what produced a bogus 'last tab 238px out of reach' reading. Measure after the animation settles.

  (j) IMAGES ARE PARTLY DONE ALREADY: 105 of the 212 live items have an image_url. Spot-checked three straight from Supabase — all valid webp (magic 52494646 / 'WEBP', ~90-120KB), so they were uploaded after the Buffer->Blob fix and are NOT corrupt.

  (k) THEN THE SHOP REVERSED (g): they did not like the flat, unfinished look of cards with no image well next to cards with photos, and asked for the shop logo as a stand-in. 40092b0 puts the 4:3 well back and fills it with /uploads/logo-8dc1f126.webp on a warm gradient when image is null. The placeholder is decorative — empty alt + aria-hidden — because naming it after the dish would lie to a screen reader. So the current behaviour is LOGO PLACEHOLDER, not 'no well'; do not 'restore' 7720352.
note_2026_08_06_delivery_copy: Same day, after the menu publish: reworked the /delivery welcome screen and the payment wording, driven entirely by the shop reviewing screenshots on their phone. Worth reading before touching this copy again, because several rounds were spent removing things I had added. (1) THE WELCOME SCREEN (e502bfc). It previously showed only a hero + a button that silently fired a LINE login and then a GPS prompt. Customers met both permissions with no idea why and only learned the delivery radius afterwards — the root of the long-open complaint about far-away customers arriving from the LINE OA with no warning. Now the screen states the service, the radius, and that being outside it is not a dead end, BEFORE the button is reachable. The CTA deliberately moved OUT of PageHero: the hero is height-capped at clamp(260px,55vw,420px) so the copy would not fit, and a button inside the hero sits above its own explanation. It also filled the dead space that made the screen look unfinished on a phone. (2) RADIUS IS NOT HARDCODED. pages/delivery.js reads getShopSettings() in getServerSideProps and passes radiusKm into OrderFlow. /api/delivery-distance only reports the radius AFTER the GPS check, far too late for this screen, and a literal 5 would rot the moment the shop edits delivery_radius_km. Verified live via __NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.radiusKm = 5. (3) PAYMENT WORDING (4a5d147): customer-facing text now says 'QR ของร้าน' / "the shop's QR code" / '本店二维码' instead of PromptPay, in the order flow, the legacy CartDrawer, and the LINE order card. PromptPay is the scheme, not what the customer thinks they are scanning, and the brand name reads as a separate app they might need. Both QR alts now derive from the same label so they cannot drift. CODE COMMENTS STILL SAY PROMPTPAY ON PURPOSE — the payload really is a PromptPay Bill Payment QR, and renaming them would hide which standard lib/promptpay.js implements. (4) THE SHOP CUT MOST OF WHAT I WROTE, and was right each time. The pattern: never name LINE in this flow, because the customer is already inside LINE and the login is silent, so mentioning it describes something they never see. Removed 'กดปุ่มด้านบนเพื่อเข้าสู่ระบบด้วย LINE และแชร์ตำแหน่ง' entirely (84d37b8 — the next screen is a dedicated distance check that explains it anyway), and 'ผ่าน LINE' off step 1 (793376e). Also cut: the heading's 'ผ่าน LINE', a duplicated ร้าน in step 2 (รัศมี already means from the shop), and the lead's เลือกเมนู which repeated step 1 verbatim. LINE is still named where it carries real information — sentToShop, sendSlip, noPromptpay's contact hint, and the login-failure messages. (5) HEADING (431e9b3, then 8846e9e for step 2). 'สั่งอาหารกลับบ้าน ผ่าน LINE' echoed the hero subtitle directly above AND step 1 directly below. It became 'สั่งอาหารกลับบ้านได้เลย' — announcing the capability rather than commanding it, because customers arriving from the OA mostly do not know the shop offers this. The hero subtitle dropped its takeaway clause so the two lines stop competing. Register note from the shop: use 'ทางร้าน' not bare 'ร้าน' when the shop refers to itself, and 'สามารถ...ได้' is right for a factual condition (step 2) but reads like an official notice in a heading. (6) FOOTER TAGLINE ALIGNMENT (94faceb). .footer-tagline had text-align:center while every other row in the footer — icons, copyright, brand — starts on the same left edge, so it visibly floated (text began 40px in on mobile, 118px in at 696px). The centring was masking a second fact rather than fixing it: the line NEVER fills its container at any width (236px slack at 696px) because the clamp is kept deliberately small — the tagline is nowrap inside overflow-hidden, so an oversized clamp CLIPS the text instead of wrapping it. Left-aligned, the slack reads as ragged-right. Fixed in BOTH styles/globals.css and site.css (the standalone HTML build keeps its own copy of the rule; they had already drifted apart in comments).

note_2026_07_30: Built the MENU BULK-IMPORT feature end to end in 5 phases, following the spec in ~/lovepier/lovep/ (233 real menu rows across 10 categories). PHASE 1 (DB, applied to prod): menu_items.import_code (unique), sub_category, status, price_original, note_internal, image_version, image_file; categories.category_no; menu_imports audit table; 10 NEW import categories seeded is_active=FALSE so they stay hidden. drizzle-kit generate is UNUSABLE (snapshot drift — orders/customers/settings/events were made via db:push), so migrations are hand-written idempotent SQL in lib/db/migrations/manual/0002_*.sql and 0003_*.sql applied via scripts/apply-menu-import-migration.mjs. PHASE 2 (lib/menuImport/{spec,parse,apply,diff}.ts + /preview): SheetJS parse of the 'menu' sheet, 19 exact headers, incomplete rows imported but forced status=planned + is_available=false rather than rejected; diff by import_code; blank optional cell = leave existing alone, so re-upload = all unchanged. PHASE 3 (imageMatch/imageProcess + /image-urls, /process-images): browser uploads originals straight to Supabase via SIGNED UPLOAD URLs (bypassing Vercel's 4.5MB body limit), server downloads each raw file, sharp -> 480/960/1440 webp, writes menu/{import_code}/{size}.webp, deletes the raw, bumps image_version. PHASE 4 (commit.ts + /commit): one transaction, upsert by import_code, update ONLY fields present in the file, menus missing from the file are NEVER deleted. Verified with 3 real commits (created=233, then unchanged=233 idempotent, then updated=1). The 233 rows ARE IN PROD (menu_items 60->293), all hidden, image_url null. featureAreas.status: fixed end to end 2026-08-06 (cbb4d6b + 40029ca); verified live
featureAreas.notes: Two independent bugs stacked on the same symptom. (a) sharp cannot decode iPhone HEIC (no HEVC in this build) -> now converted to JPEG client-side with heic2any inside lib/upload-image.ts, which every upload caller shares. (b) Server uploads passed a Node Buffer to supabase-js, which Vercel's runtime coerced to a UTF-8 string, destroying the binary (bytes >=0x80 -> EF BF BD) so files returned 200 but rendered broken — PROD ONLY, localhost never reproduced it. Always pass `new Blob([new Uint8Array(buf)], {type})`. Images uploaded before 40029ca are permanently corrupt and must be re-uploaded. EventModal now also catches upload errors instead of swallowing them.

A blank date field posts '' and `?? null` does not convert it (''  is not nullish), so '' hit the `date` column and Postgres threw 'Invalid time value' — surfaced only as a generic 'เกิดข้อผิดพลาด'. Use `|| null` for date columns. POST and PUT now also try/catch and return the real DB error, which the admin toast displays.

featureAreas.notes: Single linear wizard on /delivery: welcome -> distance check -> menu -> summary -> payment -> success. Full-screen; site nav/footer hidden during steps 2-6 via lib/chrome.js. Out-of-radius customers must tick an acknowledgement. Delivery fee is recomputed server-side in /api/orders and never trusted from the client. The WELCOME step (step 1) is the only step that still shows the site nav and footer, which is why it needed its own fit work: it is now `min-h-[calc(100dvh-var(--nav-h,64px))] sm:min-h-0` with the CTA on mt-auto + env(safe-area-inset-bottom), so the footer starts at or below the fold instead of peeking as a half-cut black band. Its hero uses PageHero's `compact` mode. To exercise steps 2-6 locally, blank NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFF_ID and use the distance step's test-mode simulate buttons — see note_2026_08_10 (0).

Default stays exactly as it was: clamp(260px, 55vw, 420px), eyebrow, 8 slide dots — used by events, gallery, about, reservation, activities, promotion. `compact` is passed ONLY by the delivery welcome and changes four things: height becomes clamp(190px, 34vh, 300px) (viewport HEIGHT, because a short screen is what squeezes that page, not a narrow one), the eyebrow is dropped, the slide dots are dropped, and the scrim goes from-black/70 via-black/35 so white type survives bright photos. The autoplay now also respects prefers-reduced-motion for ALL pages, which it previously did not (only the home page hero did).

The real app lives in love-pier-main/, built via a custom buildCommand in vercel.json that cd's into it. Vercel's framework detection runs at the repo root, so the root package.json declares next@16.2.6 and installCommand is 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund' (NOT 'echo skip' — CLI 56.x reads the version from installed node_modules). outputDirectory stays love-pier-main/.next.
Both render components/menu/MenuExperience.js (single source of truth), so menu-layout edits apply to both. Visual polish committed in 3988910.

gotchas: Server-side Supabase Storage uploads MUST pass a Blob, never a Node Buffer — Vercel coerces a Buffer body to UTF-8 and destroys the binary. Prod-only; localhost will not reproduce it.
sharp here has no HEVC decoder, so HEIC must be converted in the browser (heic2any). HEIC files often report an empty MIME type, so check the extension too.
For `date` columns, '' must become null — `?? null` does NOT do that, use `|| null`.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* env vars are inlined at BUILD time; setting them in Vercel needs a rebuild, and code must not gate behavior on them being present.
New Tailwind v4 @theme tokens can look applied in source while the utility was never generated — `next build` passing does not prove it. Verify with getComputedStyle in the browser.

`justify-center` on an `overflow-x-auto` row makes the LEADING items unreachable once it overflows — they sit past scrollLeft:0 and nothing can scroll to them. Use auto margins on the first/last children instead; they centre while it fits and collapse to 0 when it does not.

The dark circle with an 'N' floating over the bottom-left of every page in local screenshots is the Next.js dev indicator, not a layout bug. It is dev-only — confirmed absent from production HTML (grep for 'nextjs-portal' returns 0). Do not spend time chasing it.

The footer tagline is `whitespace-nowrap` inside `overflow-hidden`, so an over-large font CLIPS it rather than wrapping. That is why .footer-tagline's clamp is conservative and the line never fills its box — do not 'fix' the leftover space by enlarging the clamp. The rule is duplicated in styles/globals.css (Next app) and site.css (standalone HTML); change both.

To see /delivery steps 2-6 locally, blank NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFF_ID in .env.local (isLiffConfigured() goes false and handleStart falls straight through to the distance step), then use the distance step's own 'โหมดทดสอบระยะทาง' simulate buttons instead of GPS. Restore .env.local afterwards, and never press the final pay button — it creates a real order and pushes a LINE card.

A percentage `height` (even `height:100%`) resolves against the parent's `height` property, NOT its used height. A parent sized by flex or by `min-height` has `height:auto`, so the child computes to 0 and silently disappears. Stretch it with flex instead, or size it in vh.

Size anything in the LINE in-app browser against viewport HEIGHT, not width. LINE's own chrome eats ~45px, so a layout that just fits at 402x784 in a normal browser is below the fold there; a vw-based clamp gives a tall phone the same cramped band as a short one.

--nav-h is published by whichever chrome is sticky at the top: the site Nav on normal pages, OrderFlow's StepHeader on /delivery (Layout unmounts the Nav there). Anything new that sticks below it must offset by --nav-h, and any new top chrome must publish it and clear it on unmount.
drizzle-kit generate is unusable (snapshot drift); write idempotent SQL under lib/db/migrations/manual/ instead.
The in-app Browser pane fights ScrollStack + Lenis smooth scroll: scrollTo drifts. To screenshot a mid-page section, hide the other .scroll-stack__panel elements and add .is-visible to .reveal.

Reading scrollTop/getBoundingClientRect right after setting a scroll returns the PRE-scroll value, because scroll-behavior is smooth — this reads as 'the pane cannot scroll' and it is wrong. Wait ~1-2s or set style.scrollBehavior='auto' before measuring. Local /menu also reports offsetHeight 0 for real cards mid-HMR; measure on production when the numbers look impossible.
~/.npm has root-owned files — install with `--cache <writable dir>`.
